context_build.causal_mechanism: Verified fact: overnight CORRA is 2.29 as of 2026-09-17 and the equal-weight 2027H-Z CRA strip (2027-03 3.13, 2027-06 3.365, 2027-09 3.51, 2027-12 3.595) averages 3.40, or +111bp from overnight. August Canadian CPI-trim is 1.9 percent and CPI-median 2.0 percent with headline stuck at 3.0 percent; employment fell 42k, average hourly wages slowed to +2.0 percent y/y from +2.8 percent, and unemployment is 6.4 percent. Inference: a re-tightening cycle of that size is an energy-pass-through and imported-hawkishness assumption, not a labor/core reaction function. Soft labor and at-target underlying CPI should cap, delay, or cancel most of the priced 2027 hikes, so implied 2027 CORRA reprices lower. Unknown: the exact BoC reaction to a renewed oil spike versus a further jobs contraction.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified fact: CA 2Y yield is 3.27 as of 2026-09-17, +31bp over 1m, -4bp over 5d, -8bp over 1d, 97.8th 1y percentile. CA 2s10s is 56bp, 0.6th 1y percentile. Near-term 1m CORRA only prices +29bp by 2026-12 (implied 2.58) while 3m 2026-12 is 2.775 (+48.5bp) and 2027-03 is already 3.13 (+84bp). Inference: the last month's sovereign selloff and the 2027 strip are the market's way of embedding a 2027 hike cycle after the Sep 2 BoC energy-pass-through minutes and the global hawkish turn (Fed +25bp to 3.75-4.00 percent, BoJ to 1.25 percent). The 1d/5d 2Y dip is the first pullback from that hawkish repricing, not yet a completed fade. Unknown: how much of the 1m +31bp was energy-beta versus genuine BoC path revision.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: BoC already flagged higher energy pass-through in the Sep 2 FAD minutes; headline CPI at 3.0 percent was already in the tape; Fed hike odds were >90 percent into Sep 16 and the hike was delivered. New enough to keep the trade live: August employment -42k and wage deceleration to 2.0 percent, trim/median still at 1.9/2.0, Saudi workaround reducing the extreme oil-supply tail on 2026-09-16, and the 2027H-Z strip still marking 3.40 rather than the 2.3-2.8 near-term corridor. Inference: the known energy narrative is still what holds 2027 implied rates up; the labor/core state is the under-weighted new information. Round-2 CAD-higher pitches recycle that known energy/activity narrative as if it were a fresh catch-up catalyst. The last24 desk thesis that the energy shock constrains global easing is the priced story, not a fresh catalyst.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: CORRA futures imply the BoC takes overnight from 2.29 to about 2.58 by Dec 2026 and then through 3.13/3.365/3.51/3.595 across 2027H-Z, with a terminal near 3.65 in 2028. That requires energy pass-through and/or imported tightening to dominate a labor market that is already contracting and core inflation that is already at the 2 percent target. Independent US path (SOFR 3.85, SR3 2027-09 4.755, +90.5bp) is priced as a continuing hike cycle; Canada is priced as catching a large part of that hawkish impulse with a lag.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that Canada delivers anything like +111bp into 2027H-Z. The priced assumption — and the CAD-higher opponents’ assumption — is that headline 3 percent plus BoC energy-pass-through minutes plus Fed/BoJ hawkishness plus lagged activity 66 force a hike cycle and a CAD bid. The disagreed assumption is that trim/median at target and a -42k / 2.0 percent wage labor market cannot sustain that path; 2027 implied CORRA should fall toward a hold or shallow-hike profile closer to the 2026 1m strip than to mid-3s.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: overnight 2.29 (easy versus SOFR 3.85 and AONIA 4.35). Change: 1m CORRA is almost unchanged into October (+1.5bp) then +14bp Nov and +29bp Dec; the 3m curve then steepens into 2027 (Mar +84bp, Jun +107.5bp, Sep +122bp, Dec +130.5bp). The 2027H-Z average of 3.40 is the hike-cycle component. Sovereign CA 2Y at 3.27 sits between the 2027-03 contract (3.13) and 2027-06 (3.365), so the 2Y percentile stretch is the same policy-path story, not a separate term-premium event. CA-US 2Y at -140bp (3.8th 1y / 4.3rd 5y percentile) shows Canada already cheap versus the US; the remaining mispricing is intra-Canada 2027 versus overnight/labor, not a CA-US catch-up that still needs more Canadian hikes. 1d CA 2Y -8bp is the marginal driver this snapshot, not a new 10Y term-premium shock (CA 10Y 3.83, -9bp 1d).

analogs: Closest mechanism analog is an energy-headline versus core-and-labor split: 2015-16 BoC looked through an oil-driven headline CPI gap while the labor market softened, and a front-end hike-cycle pricing that was not validated by domestic slack subsequently faded. Forward outcome in that class of episodes is lower implied policy rates once employment and wages, not headline CPI, become the binding constraint.

No packet-sourced episode is an exact 2026 match; treat the analog as the transmission channel (look-through of energy into a hiking path that labor cannot bear), not as a numerical template. Value-guy’s 2025-01-30 CA-US compression analog is not a Canada-hike analog; the 2024-12-18 widening analog they also cite keeps the peer-spread two-sided.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Overnight CORRA is already 2.29, so this is a fade of a re-tightening cycle from an easy starting point, not a 2022-style fade from highly restrictive real rates. The Sep 2 BoC energy-pass-through minutes and the still-alive energy-shock-absorber warning are a live hawk channel. Q2 real GDP +0.8 percent q/q and a 66 activity score are lagged offsets that were not present in a classic labor-collapse analog. US policy is hiking (funds 3.75-4.00, SR3 peak 4.755), which can import financial-condition tightness into Canada even if the BoC stays on hold.

Energy-narrative check: BoC minutes flag pass-through risk, but the 2026-09-16 Saudi workaround reduces the extreme oil-supply tail even as a separate rollup warns that energy shock absorbers are weakening. That split is why 2027 implied rates can stay elevated without labor confirmation.

INFERENCE: hawks and CAD-higher seats are treating energy pass-through, lagged activity 66, and Fed/BoJ tightening as sufficient to re-tighten Canada into the mid-3s and bid CAD; labor and underlying CPI say that cycle will not be delivered, so 2027 implied CORRA falls. UNKNOWN: whether a renewed oil spike or a strong Q3 GDP follow-through on the +0.8 percent Q2 print can keep the BoC on a hiking path despite jobs. Actionable expression: stay long the existing 2027H-Z strip.
revised_trade.mispricing: The 2027H-Z average of 3.40 requires the BoC to deliver roughly four 25bp hikes from 2.29 into 2027. Near-term 1m pricing only has +29bp by Dec 2026, so the mispricing is concentrated in 2027 delivery, not in the next two announcements. That 2027 premium is the energy-pass-through / catch-up assumption, not the labor/core state. CRAH27 at 3.13 is not an underpriced front; it is the first step of an already-steep 2027 path.
why_now: August jobs -42k and wage deceleration to 2.0 percent are contemporaneous; the 2027 strip has not marked that softness (still 3.40).

Headline 3.0 percent with trim 1.9 / median 2.0 keeps the BoC energy story in the minutes without giving it a core inflation mandate; CAD-higher seats are recycling that known minutes risk as a hike catalyst.
The 2026-09-16 Saudi workaround reduces the extreme oil-supply tail that was supporting hike-cycle pricing even as a separate energy-absorber warning remains.
CA 2Y already -8bp on the day from a 1m +31bp selloff: the hawkish repricing is starting to crack at the sovereign front end while the 2027 strip is unchanged at the prior 3.40 book mark.

attack: The strongest opposing claim is Canada-too-easy catch-up: pay 2027 CORRA and buy CAD because overnight 2.29, headline 3.0, activity 66, energy minutes, and CA-US 2Y at -140bp mean the BoC must hike. That substitutes a lagged activity print and a peer-spread percentile for the binding contemporaneous constraint. FACT: trim 1.9 / median 2.0 and employment -42k / wages 2.0 percent / unemployment 6.4 percent. INFERENCE: the BoC does not have a core-inflation mandate to deliver four 25bp hikes into 2027. Energy pass-through is flagged in minutes, not observed in core. Paying CRAH27 at 3.13 while 2027-09/12 already print 3.51/3.595 is paying the first step of a cycle this seat fades at the 3.40 average.

CAD-higher is a weaker expression of the same bad assumption. FACT: USDCAD is already 74th 1y / 87th 5y after +1.74 percent over 1m; packet USDCAD~CA-US_2Y r-squared is 0.022. INFERENCE: the dollar pair has already paid a lot of the 'Canada is easy' story, and the RV does not map into CAD. Cross-merchant can be right on AUD/housing without CAD rising. Positioning-cynic has no CFTC on CRA. Mean-reverter’s USD-lower is a US SOFR receive after a fully priced hike; even if that fade is right, it does not force CAD higher or validate 2027 CORRA at 3.40. UNKNOWN: post-2026-09-18 FX ticks versus cutoff 2026-09-20T19:39:35Z.

Imported hawkishness (rate-hawk short SOFR_2027-09 at 4.755; trend-follower short SOFR_2027-03 at 4.58) can keep USD bid versus CAD. It does not require the BoC to catch a 156bp overnight gap while Canadian labor is 38 and US labor is 75. The CA-US 2Y is already at a 3.8th percentile; that is the imported-hawkishness price, not unused CAD catch-up.
defense: FACT: sidecar already owns long CORRA_2027H-Z pos-9849cf751c27 at entry 3.4, 85m notional, 850k standard-shock risk capital versus a 10m cap; packet mark is still 3.40. INFERENCE: Round-2 currency tags did not move the object of the trade. USD-higher / CAD-lower were residual mappings of an undelivered BoC cycle versus a still-hiking Fed, not a spot expression. The rates candidate remains cleaner, so the seat stays long duration / expected_mark_direction lower. Carry supports if overnight stays nearer 2.29 than 3.40. UNKNOWN: street CRA positioning.

Would concede the argument if the BoC delivers or credibly commits to the priced 2027 mid-3s path, or if CPI-trim/median leave the 1.9-2.0 percent area while employment stops contracting. A Q3 GDP follow-through that repairs labor, or an oil spike that broadens into core, would also break the fade. A US duration rally alone would not. A CAD rally that leaves 2027H-Z at 3.40 would not. Flattening to dodge SOFR vig is not a concession: funded-seat vig accrues on the 100m allocation either way.

Book decision is HOLD of pos-9849cf751c27. Do not OPEN a duplicate strip. Do not ADD: energy pass-through remains the live hawk risk and 9.15m unused shock budget is the buffer. Do not CLOSE: the 2027 hike-cycle discrepancy versus labor/core is intact at the same packet mark.
